claim_summary: KairosAgent contributes a tool-using temporal reasoner, a trajectory corpus and turn-level training, and a morphology-conditioned forecasting procedure that feeds qualitative reasoning into a TSFM.

claim_evidence.quote: We propose K AIROS AGENT, an agentic multimodal time series forecasting framework that bridges semantic reasoning and numerical forecasting by deducing future morphology and integrating it into the forecasting pipeline.

We curate T-STAR, a 40k-trajectory time series reasoning corpus with tool augmentation, and introduce turn-level credit assignment for RL to provide fine-grained supervision beyond sparse outcome-level rewards.

modules.name: Tool-grounded morphology reasoner training
modules.scope_reason: R2 places SFT and RL parameter updates on the LLM side because they train morphology responses and tool/action selection.

evidence.quote: We warm up the reasoner via SFT on T-STAR trajectories, formatting each as a multi-turn chat containing system instructions, user queries, tool interactions, and the morphology description.
To enhance reasoning quality, we refine the reasoner using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) (Shao et al., 2024), employing the frozen Stage II forecaster as a reward module.

modules.name: Windowed statistical analysis tool suite
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK is no: generic statistics do not embed a task-family output criterion. R3_2_GTS is yes: the tools operate on temporal history windows and compute temporal statistics; they are task-agnostic.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - general windowed statistics do not encode a task criterion

evidence.quote: The agent is equipped with 23 statistical analysis tools adapted from tsfresh (Christ et al., 2018). All tools operate on a user-specified window [left, right) of the history, allowing the agent to inspect both global and local temporal structures.

modules.name: Morphology-conditioned forecasting bridge
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK is yes: this procedure fuses morphology into a numerical forecasting model; changing the task changes its forecast objective and output head.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - conditions a numerical forecasting output on morphology

evidence.quote: We introduce a lightweight fusion operator that integrates the semantic prior into the decoder of Kairos.
We retain its encoder-decoder backbone and prediction head, but augment it with a text adapter

modules.name: T-STAR tool-use trajectory corpus
modules.scope_reason: R2 places this trajectory corpus on the LLM side because it is built to train morphology responses and tool-calling behavior.

evidence.quote: We construct T-STAR, a tool-augmented corpus comprising over 40k validated examples drawn from 29 datasets across nine domains.
each T-STAR example records the full reasoning trajectory of a tool-calling agent, including multi-turn tool calls, tool responses, and a natural-language morphology forecast

process_validity.quote: Samples failing any check are retried up to 3 times. Samples that remain invalid after all retries are discarded. This pipeline ensures that retained trajectories exhibit correct tool usage, grounded reasoning, and morphologically accurate forecasts.

temporal_validity.quote: and the train/validation/test partitions are chronological 60%/20%/20% splits.

task_performance.quote: For reasoning evaluation, we report Accuracy as judged by the LLM-as-a-judge protocol.

notes: The statistical tool suite is separate from the task-bound forecasting bridge: its temporal-window inputs and statistics are reusable in principle, while the source applies the system only to forecasting.
